headline.title: Five companies beat last night, and what separated the winners from the losers was not the beat — it was the margin. GTLB +23.3% printed a 15% operating margin against 11.2% consensus. DELL +9.1% raised full-year sales guidance by $25 billion. On the other side, CRDO −10.5% beat both lines and got sold because non-GAAP gross margin came in at 68.0% against 68.3% expected, and PANW −1.8% beat with Next-Gen Security ARR up 64% but the headline read margins narrow. MDB −12.0% beat and raised, and lost because Atlas growth held at 29% instead of accelerating.
headline.summary: Margin expansion is being paid, margin compression is being sold, and a beat by itself buys nothing. That is a sharper rule than hardware-versus-software, and it survives every one of last night's five prints. DELL's number was scale — EPS $7.04 against $4.90, revenue $47B against $44.7B, AI server revenue doubled to $16.4B with orders at $60.9B, and strength running well beyond AI into traditional servers, networking, storage and PCs. HPE +4.3% and NTAP +2.1% ride that read into their own prints tonight. The AI-adjacent complex is broadly lower with them: DDOG −3.3%, MRVL −1.6%, SMTC −1.2%, ALAB −1.2%. Macro offers nothing: the 10-year is up 2bp to 4.81%, VIX +2.4% to 16.73, Brent $95.11. BOJ Governor Ueda signalled a hike could come this month and Asia broke — KOSPI −3.99%, Nikkei −2.85%. New Zealand hiked 25bp overnight.

overview: Everything today points at one report, and last night set the bar it has to clear. AVGO reports after the close carrying an 8.4% implied move — more than double any other Mag 11 name — into a tape that just proved a beat is worth nothing without margin behind it. Its Tuesday candle is a Failed 2D, the second straight session it and NVDA both printed one. Meanwhile the index has stopped trending: SPY, QQQ and IWM each printed a third consecutive 2 Down Tuesday, but all three are trading inside Tuesday's range this morning rather than below it — no continuation trigger, a coil into the Beige Book at 1:00pm CT. The rotation underneath is real and it is not AI: travel and cruise lines are bid across the board into Trump's 11:30am meeting with U.S. travel executives, and gold and silver miners are bid alongside the yield move. The one Mag 11 name in a clean uptrend is AAPL, a 2 Up that closed +2.61% on John Ternus's first day and is extending on the cheapest premium on the board.
setups: The prep sheet's double-star. Tuesday was a 2 Down that closed 425.00 near its low; the blowout gaps it to 465.99 and through Tuesday's 463.00 high — a 2-2 reversal up, almost a bullish kicker. The trigger is calls above $474, and that level is a real shelf: Monday's high was 474.49, Friday's 474.74. Allow price to show its hands — the 6HR is still inside, and if it consolidates here that is the tell worth watching.

Tuesday took Monday's 321.235 high to 327.30 and closed 325.13, +2.61%, on John Ternus's first day as CEO. 3 bar on the 6HR. The trigger is calls above $327.30 for the 2-2U — premarket 326.80 sits just under it. In a Mag 11 where MSFT, AMD, INTC and MU are all lower, this is the one name with a structure, and the 9/4 straddle implies only 1.95%, the cheapest on the board.

Not on the prep sheet, but it is the day's gravity. Tuesday broke Monday's 366.30 low to 362.00 and closed 369.68 back above — a Failed 2D. The 9/4 straddle prices 8.4%, more than double any other Mag 11 name. It reports into a tape that sold three beats last night, and the bar it has to clear is not a beat, it is margin. The event is tonight; today is positioning, not the trade.

Investor briefing tomorrow, and it lands in the afternoon. Note the earlier week-ahead calendar had it Wednesday; the prep sheet puts it Thursday, and Fal.Con itself closed 9/1, so Thursday is the consistent read.
Premarket 214.70, −0.2%. It closed 215.07 Tuesday, having given back most of Monday's +5.79% Fal.Con run.
An afternoon event means it could simply consolidate through tomorrow. The move usually shows up in the two sessions after the investor day, not on the day itself.

That is a problem for 9/4 contracts. With the briefing Thursday afternoon, the two-day move window is Friday 9/4 and — because Monday 9/7 is Labor Day — Tuesday 9/8. A 9/4 expiry dies at the close of day one of that window and gets no second day at all.

Next week's contracts are a lot safer here, and 9/11 exists. It covers both sessions of the expected move plus buffer, and it does not pay for the consolidation. Keep next week in mind — the event is tomorrow but the trade is after it.

Listed as the day's thesis, not a trade. The rule that fits all five prints: margin expansion paid, compression sold, a beat alone worth nothing. That is what AVGO has to clear tonight.

Against that, XLE printed a Failed 2U on Tuesday's candle and ran 60% puts at ~3.4× average. XLE is −0.4% premarket, BP −1.9%, XOM −1.0%.
A $182M bullish block in the biggest services name, against a topping signal and put flow in the sector ETF. Both are real and they point opposite ways.
Energy has run three sessions on the Hormuz premium and Brent is already $94-95. A Failed 2U at the top of that run is exactly where the trade ends.
Not a trade today — a warning. The single-name block may simply be dividend-related positioning. When the sector ETF tops and the flow splits, the resolution comes from price, not from either ticket.

darkpool.note: Tuesday's tape leaned bid where the size stacked up — index ETFs and mega-cap tech — and leaned ask in exactly one corner: memory. SPY was the single biggest line on the entire board at $6.7B cumulative bid, with QQQ $4.5B bid top-three, and the largest single print on the tape was SPYM $1.0B bid. Ex-ETF, NVDA led twice — the biggest single-name print at $761M bid and cumulative flow $4.9B bid, by a mile. Right behind it sat the other side of the same trade: MU $4.4B ask and SNDK $3.1B ask, with WDC $406M ask rounding out the memory/storage theme. Institutions bought the index and the GPU and sold the memory complex. The options tape split just as cleanly. The largest block on either board was $182.3M of SLB $42.5C 09/18, a crossed floor ticket and a loud bullish-energy footprint — against the largest sweeps being long-dated downside, $4.9M of QQQ $677P 11/30 and $2.9M of ANET $190P 01/21/28. A $182M energy call block versus index and semi put sweeps is genuinely mixed, which is the honest read into a Fed-heavy, oil-driven week. Two filters back names already on this sheet: AAPL lit Unusual Options Volume at 56% calls across 28 prints, and Options Above Average flagged DELL at 65% calls, ~6.8× average and HPE 76% bullish, ~3.7× into their catalysts. XLE went the other way at 60% puts, ~3.4× — and XLE also printed a Failed 2U, which is the first real topping tell in the energy trade. Odd name out: SUNB $453M, an equipment-rental company that rarely prints this size, #7 ex-ETF and one of the ≤3-print concentrated names alongside WDC, MA, WFC and BRK.B.
